headline: Broad egress plus shared API/file surfaces create medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; no direct pairwise evidence is available.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest external content through MCP/direct function calls and broad network egress, while RD-Agent can run browsers and call LLM APIs. That makes a plausible path where content from one agent is treated as instructions by the other, especially via shared files or copied outputs. No direct pairwise proof exists, so uncertainty is escalated to medium.
conditions: IF aci outputs browser-sourced or API-sourced text into a shared channel, THEN RD-Agent can parse it as instructions.
IF both agents are connected through an MCP server or shared workspace, THEN prompt content can bridge between them.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of one agent's raw outputs by the other.
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.
Route inter-agent handoff through a human review step.
Restrict browser-sourced content to quoted excerpts only.
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitizing adapters between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad egress; RD-Agent touches financial reports, datasets, logs, and sends data to external LLM APIs. If they share files or a workspace, sensitive material from either side can flow into the other's outbound requests. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default-style integrations, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem or workspace, THEN data from one can be read by the other.
IF RD-Agent forwards its context to OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek APIs, THEN any shared sensitive inputs can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent.
Remove sensitive files from any shared directory.
Turn off unnecessary outbound connectors for both agents.
Review logs for accidental inclusion of CRM or financial data.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both have broad network egress, while aci can write through CRM/email/calendar APIs and RD-Agent writes logs and uses external APIs. Overlapping mutable surfaces create coordination and overwrite risk if they operate on the same resources. The profiles do not prove a shared lock or shared target, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same CRM, email, or project directory, THEN concurrent writes can conflict.
IF either agent runs without external locking, THEN last-write-wins overwrites are possible.
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource scopes to each agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared state.
Use per-resource locks where available.
Limit one agent to read-only access during coordination.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks on shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and RD-Agent can consume outputs while also taking research actions through APIs and browser workflows. If RD-Agent treats aci's outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade from one agent into downstream actions. The profiles show a plausible handoff but not a verified verification step, so medium fits.
conditions: IF RD-Agent uses aci-generated summaries as inputs without verification, THEN incorrect facts can propagate.
IF aci produces CRM or email actions that RD-Agent later operationalizes, THEN downstream mistakes can multiply.
mitigations: Require source citations before RD-Agent acts on aci output.
Add a human approval gate for any action-taking step.
Compare outputs against original records before execution.
Keep aci outputs as suggestions, not commands.
requires-engineering: implement automated cross-checking between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, and support data, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, datasets, and logs and sends data to third-party LLM APIs. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch around retention, residency, or regulated data handling if the same sensitive class is routed through both. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated customer or financial data is routed from aci into RD-Agent prompts, THEN retention and third-party processing obligations may be triggered.
IF either agent logs sensitive inputs, THEN retention policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Classify data before handing it between agents.
Exclude regulated records from RD-Agent prompts.
Shorten log retention on both systems.
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for regulated data.
